summary: The study investigates the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of TiO2 using TiI4 and H2O-H2O2 precursors. The growth mechanism is primarily temperature-dependent, with the reaction of H2O-H2O2 with the TiI4-terminated surface being self-limiting. The process involves alternating pulses of the precursors, with the growth rate influenced by temperature and precursor doses. The study highlights the formation of anatase and rutile phases at different temperatures and the role of surface reactions in determining the film structure.
evidence: Atomic layer deposition of TiO2 films from alternate pulses of TiI4 and H2O-H2O2 vapors was studied with a quartz crystal microbalance in real time. The reaction of H2O-H2O2 with the TiIx-terminated surface was a self-limited process. The film growth rate increased with the increase of the substrate temperature from 200 to 300 °C. At temperatures above 300 °C, the growth rate was again almost invariant. The study also discusses the formation of anatase and rutile phases at different temperatures.
